positive.prompt: Walk me through this codebase, I'm new here
I never really understood how the build pipeline works, teach me from scratch
We just merged the big refactor — give me a walkthrough of what the system looks like now
Help me understand this architecture before I touch it

negative.prompt: Review this diff before I merge it
Write a failing test for this bug before fixing it

evals.prompt: I just joined this project and I'm lost. What is the orchestration layer actually doing? Why are there two config systems? And what's a "gate contract" — everyone keeps saying it but nobody explains it. Walk me through it properly.
evals.expected_output: A single-reply coaching response that reduces the three questions to one stated, verifiable missing-prerequisite hypothesis (or explicitly queues them), defines the coined term before it carries weight, advances one cognitive center, and ends with a specific relation/fork check — not three answer sections and not a bare 'does that make sense?'
expectations: The reply reduces the questions to a stated hypothesis about a common missing prerequisite (e.g. how configuration flows end to end) and names it as a hypothesis the user can correct — or explicitly queues them with one taught first — rather than answering each question in its own section

The coined term ('gate contract') is defined in place, confirmed as known, or explicitly placeholdered before it carries argumentative weight; it is never assumed known just because 'everyone says it'
Exactly one cognitive center is advanced in this first reply
The reply ends by checking a specific relation, distinction, or next fork — not a bare 'does that make sense?'
Load-bearing claims either cite reviewable anchors (real file/type/method names) with implementation and evidence status labeled, or are explicitly marked as inference/unverified
No scenario-style metaphor (characters as subjects, role interaction); any metaphor is a one-sentence naming-style mapping, and plain statement dominates
